mission_09: Outstanding work implementing the Listen, Attend and Spell architecture! You now understand one of the foundational end-to-end speech recognition models that eliminated the need for separate acoustic, pronunciation, and language models. The bidirectional encoder captures rich contextual representations by processing audio in both temporal directions, giving the model access to both past and future context at every time step. The Bahdanau attention mechanism learns a soft alignment between audio frames and output characters, automatically discovering which parts of the audio are relevant for generating each character without any explicit alignment supervision. The autoregressive decoder generates text one character at a time, with each prediction conditioned on the full history through the decoder state and on the relevant audio through the attention context. The end-to-end training with cross-entropy loss jointly optimizes all components, allowing the model to learn representations that are specifically tailored for the transcription task. This architecture paved the way for modern ASR systems and demonstrated that neural networks could learn the complete speech-to-text pipeline from raw features to text.
